anomalies.obs: On the /Microcontroller/ sheet the WS2812B status LED D5 pin 4 (DIN) is wired only to the net NET0004, and NET0004 appears nowhere else on the schematic. anomalies.expected: The spec lists a working onboard WS2812B status LED (D1) driven by firmware (led.rs); its DIN must be connected to an ESP32 GPIO so the MCU can clock data into it.

evidence.quote: /Microcontroller/ sheet: D5 WS2812B pin 4 DIN -> NET0004; U6 GPIO8 (23) and GPIO9 (24) have no label/wire; NET0004 has a single endpoint (D5.4).
Exposes status over Wi-Fi via a small webserver ... and a single onboard WS2812B status LED (D1).

anomalies.impact: The status LED data line is floating, so the WS2812B never receives valid data; the onboard status indication described in the spec does not work.

anomalies.obs: On the /Microcontroller/ sheet the USB-C receptacle power pin J10 A4 is labelled VBUS, while on the /Power/ sheet the TPS2121 mux U10 IN2 (pin 2) is on the +5V net and its OUT (pin 1) is on the VBUS net (the same name as the USB pin). The +5V net therefore has no driver, and the USB VBUS pin carries the same name as the mux output / buck input rail.
anomalies.expected: Spec: USB VBUS pins feed the +5V net which goes to the mux IN2, and the mux OUT is a separate VBUS net. i.e. A4 -> +5V, mux OUT -> VBUS, two distinct nets.

evidence.quote: /Microcontroller/: J10 A4 -> VBUS. /Power/: U10 IN2(2) -> +5V, U10 OUT(1) -> VBUS.
J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2) ... outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net ... distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux.

anomalies.impact: The USB-C supply is not routed to the mux's IN2 input (the +5V net is undriven), so the autoswitching power path described in the spec is broken; depending on label scope the mux output rail and the USB VBUS pin are also merged, risking back-feed of the unregulated rail into the USB port.

anomalies.obs: On the /Microcontroller/ sheet the TPS1H200 heater switch U4 has a +3V3 connection (junction dot to a +3V3 arrow) at its IN/DIAG_EN pin pair, while only one of those pins carries the GPIO1 control net NET0003.
anomalies.expected: Spec: the heater switch is driven by ESP32 GPIO1 on both IN and DIAG_EN; neither control pin should be hard-tied to +3V3.

evidence.quote: /Microcontroller/: U4 TPS1H200AQDGNRQ1 pins 1/2 (IN, DIAG_EN) show a +3V3 junction together with the NET0003 label.
driven by ESP32 GPIO1 on both IN and DIAG_EN

anomalies.impact: With the switch's IN tied to +3V3 instead of GPIO1, the heater output is permanently enabled and GPIO1 can no longer switch the load, defeating the bang-bang heater control.
